subject: Lumidex pilot — post-call recap & boarding plan
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ava Collins <ava.collins@lumidex.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 14 Feb 2026 15:22:00 -0800
Subject: Lumidex pilot — post-call recap & boarding plan

Hi Ava,

Thanks again for a productive discovery today — appreciate you walking us through the content discovery use case and the examples of where inference latency and hallucinations are currently costing Lumidex time in your customer support flow. Quick recap from our side so we’re aligned before we kick off the pilot: 

Pain points we heard
- Support agents spend ~6–9 min per ticket on knowledge retrieval and summarization; inconsistent answers across agents.
- Current system times out on longer threads (above ~3k tokens), causing dropped context.
- Cost per ticket is unpredictable due to variable batch sizes and no KV caching.

Pilot goals / success metrics (30-day pilot)
- Reduce agent median time-to-resolution by 20% (target: 5 min).
- Maintain or improve answer accuracy: target 90% on Lumidex prompt eval set.
- Average end-to-end latency under 350ms p50 for short queries, p95 < 900ms.
- Per-ticket inference cost <= $0.08 (token-normalized).

Scope we propose
- Inference model: open-model variant recommended in SOW (quantized 4-bit).
- Workload: 1 rule-based prompt + 7 exemplar prompts (prompt set attached).
- Data: sample ticket corpus (4k tickets) for prompt tuning and eval.
- Integrations: temporary API key + role-based service account for Lumidex dev team.

Owners & contacts
- Lumidex: Ava Collins (PO), security lead: Rajesh Menon (separate thread for SOC2).
- Redwood: Tessa Morgan (AE, primary), Jonas Weber (Solutions Eng, infra + evals), Marissa Cole (Customer Success).

Immediate action items (next 72 hours)
1) Lumidex: Share sample ticket exports (anonymized), and confirm a service account email for API access.
2) Redwood: Share SOW + onboarding checklist (attached).
3) Both: Schedule kickoff call for Mon 17 Feb at 10:00 PT (proposed).

Attachments: Lumidex_POC_SOW_v1.pdf (SOW), redwood_onboarding_checklist.xlsx (access & infra tasks).

If any of the bullets above need edits, flag them inline and I’ll update the SOW. Otherwise I’ll circulate a short kickoff agenda and invite the Lumidex devs.

Best,

Tessa Morgan
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Lumidex pilot — post-call recap & boarding plan

Thanks Tessa — this looks great and captures what we discussed. A few clarifications from our side: 

- We can provide an anonymized export of 3,800 tickets by EOD Monday.
- Security: Rajesh will send the SOC2 questionnaire and point of contact for our security team; we need SOC2 Type II evidence before granting production-like data (we can do a sanitized dev set first).
- Timeline: the team prefers Tue 18 Feb for kickoff (10:00 PT) instead of Mon; Availabilities attached.
- Cost target: the $0.08 figure looks achievable; would like Redwood to document how caching/batching will be applied so we can forecast monthly spend.

We’ll confirm the service account email (will come from identity@lumidex.ai). Please add the DocuSign SOW link when ready so our procurement team can start review.

—Ava
Ava Collins
Head of Product Operations | Lumidex

Date: Mon, 16 Feb 2026 11:18:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Lumidex pilot — notes + infra prep

Tessa — quick internal note after reading Ava's reply. A couple of infra items for prep before they hand over samples: 

- Pre-authorize a dev-only API key scoped to ticket ingestion and eval calls; we should rotate it after the pilot. Add this to the onboarding checklist.
- Prepare a short eval harness: 200-shot prompt eval and a separate hallucination-check prompt set (we should ensure 10% of examples are adversarial).
- For latency targets, plan to enable prefix/KV caching on common ticket templates and set a max batch window of 25ms for sub-200 token queries. Document the expected P50/P95 impact in the SOW appendix.

I can draft the eval harness and a one-page infra diagram. Want me to send to Lumidex ahead of kickoff or present during the kickoff?

—Jonas
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Subject: Confirmed: Tue 18 Feb kickoff moved — agenda + access checklist (final)

Hi Ava (and team),

Thanks for the confirmations and the availability — we’ve locked in Tue 18 Feb at 10:00 PT for the kickoff. Finalized items below and a short agenda attached. Please review access steps; Rajesh, if you can confirm SOC2 evidence scope (dev-only vs production) that will unblock API key creation.

Final scope summary (agreed)
- 30-day pilot, dev dataset (anonymized 3,800 tickets), Redwood-hosted inference under a dedicated dev pool.
- Eval: 200-shot accuracy eval + 50 adversarial hallucination checks.
- Metrics: median resolution time, p50/p95 latency, accuracy on eval set, and cost-per-ticket.

Action checklist (owners & due dates)
- Lumidex: Share anonymized ticket export (Ava) — due Mon 17 Feb 18:00 PT.
- Lumidex: Confirm service account email and procurement contact (Ava / Rajesh) — due Mon 17 Feb 18:00 PT.
- Redwood: Provision dev API key & onboarding vault entry (Jonas) — done Tue 17 Feb 09:30 PT.
- Redwood: Eval harness & prompt set (Jonas) — draft ready for kickoff.
- Procurement: DocuSign SOW (Tessa) — link: https://docusign.example.com/LUM-2026-031

Access steps completed (summary)
- Dev API key provisioned to identity@lumidex.ai (temp key, expires in 45 days).
- Shared folder created: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1LumidexOnboarding (read-only to Lumidex devs for now).

Attachments: kickoff_agenda.pdf, redwood_onboarding_checklist.xlsx (updated), Lumidex_POC_SOW_v1.pdf (with pricing appendix).

Next: I’ll post a short meeting invite with the agenda and run through the eval harness on the call. Looking forward — let us know if anything else should change before Tuesday.

Best regards,

Tessa Morgan
